subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — commit sensitivity to GPU market moves
messages:
From: Elena Gutierrez <elena@aurora-ai.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: procure@aurora-ai.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 14:12:34 -0700
Subject: Capacity ask + price-protection options for upcoming commit

Hi Vivek,

We're preparing a reserved capacity commitment for the next 12 months and need Redwood's detailed sizing and pricing sensitivity. High-level: Aurora is looking at reserving the equivalent of ~10x A100-class GPUs for a 12-month term starting June. Before we lock anything down, procurement needs: 1) concrete sizing options (10, 8, 6 GPUs) with throughput & latency expectations, 2) a pricing sensitivity table showing how unit MSRP movements (+10%, +20%, -10%) would affect the effective per-GPU price under any proposed discount, and 3) contract language options for price pass-through or index-linking.

Attached is our RFP (Aurora_RFP_Q1.pdf) with expected peak Q3 usage patterns. Two constraints: we need a predictable budget envelope and some protection if GPU spot/market prices spike mid-term. We're open to tiered discounts or a short initial tenor with an automatic extension.

Can your team turn around a first-pass by end of next week (Mar 28)? Happy to jump on a quick call to align assumptions.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Gutierrez
Head of AI Platform, Aurora AI
[Attachment: Aurora_RFP_Q1.pdf (PDF, 240 KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gutierrez <elena@aurora-ai.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:18:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ask + price-protection options for upcoming commit

Elena — thanks for the RFP and the clarity. cc'ing Naomi (finance) and Karthik (infra) so we can give you both the commercial sensitivity and the technical sizing.

Quick clarifying questions before we build scenarios:
- Confirmed baseline: 10 GPUs dedicated, 12-month start June 1?
- Do you require hard SLAs for p95 latency (e.g., <150ms for gen workloads) or is throughput more important?
- Any preference on quantization/low-precision (that will change GPU equivalent counts)?

We'll put together three commitment profiles:
A) 10 GPU reserved (12 months) — highest discount assumptions
B) 8 GPU reserved (12 months) — medium discount
C) 6 GPU reserved + burst pool (12 months) — lower discount, burst priced separately

Naomi and Karthik — can you please draft a pricing-sensitivity matrix (base GPU cost delta vs effective unit price after discount) and a couple of legal clause options (index-linked passthrough vs fixed cap) for Elena?

I can deliver the first-pass term sheet + spreadsheet by EOD Mar 28.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 11:07:50 -0700
Subject: FW: Pricing sensitivity scenarios for Aurora — draft

Vivek / Karthik — draft pricing sensitivity below. Putting numbers in-line so we have something concrete to share with Elena. I'll include a chart as an attachment.

Assumptions: base internal GPU cost today = $12,000 per GPU-month (all-in for reserved A100-equivalent pool). Redwood baseline list price to customers (no commit) = $16,000 gpu-month. Discounts are applied off list per contract.

Scenario table (effective customer unit price after discount):
- Option A (10 GPUs, 12m) — proposed discount 20% off list -> base effective price = $12,800/gpu-month. Sensitivity:
  - If GPU market costs +10% => our margin falls ~40% vs target; to preserve margin we'd need to reduce discount to ~12% or trigger pass-through
  - If GPU market costs +20% => require either price pass-through clause or margin hit; suggested move: index-link with 3-month lookback and cap at +15% pass-through unless Aurora agrees to shorten tenor
- Option B (8 GPUs, 12m) — proposed discount 15% -> effective $13,600/gpu-month. More headroom for market moves; can absorb +10% cost without pass-through
- Option C (6 GPUs + burst) — proposed discount 10% -> effective $14,400/gpu-month. Burst buckets priced at on-demand with soft cap.

Commercial levers we recommend offering:
1) Tenor ladder: 6-month firm + optional 6-month extension at pre-negotiated re-price bands.
2) Index-linked pass-through: tie our unit cost to a cloud GPU market index; pass-through applies if index > baseline by threshold (e.g., 12%). Cap required for customer protection (suggest cap at 20%).
3) Usage floors + true-up: guarantee minimum utilization (e.g., 70% of reserved capacity) or pay a true-up fee.
4) Hybrid discount: larger initial commit discount but with an annual reconciliation tied to an agreed per-GPU cost band.

Risk notes: if we offer >18% discount upfront on a long 12m term without pass-through we risk negative unit margins if market supply tightens.

Uploading chart: pricing_sensitivity_chart.png

Recommend we propose Option A as Aurora asked (10 GPUs), but condition it on either: (a) index-pass-through with a reasonable cap, or (b) split tenor (6m firm + 6m option) with a reprice collar.

Naomi Feldman
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_sensitivity_chart.png (PNG, 120 KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 08:44:15 -0700
Subject: Request: approval for Aurora offer structure (discount vs pass-through)

Marissa — quick ask. Aurora (prospect) wants 10 GPUs reserved for 12 months. Naomi's sensitivity shows that a 20% upfront discount gets us close to margin thresholds if GPU market prices increase by +10–20%. Two customer-friendly structures we can offer — need finance sign-off on which we can approve: 

1) Offer A (preferred by customer) — 20% discount, 12-month firm; include index-linked pass-through with 3-month lookback; pass-through triggers if index > baseline by 12%; cap pass-through at +20% over baseline.

2) Offer B (lower risk) — 15% discount, 12-month firm; include usage floor 70% + year-end reconciliation; no pass-through.

Naomi recommends Offer B if finance prefers predictable exposure. I think Offer A wins the deal but increases our upside risk unless capped. We need a one-line approval (A or B) and any caveats for legal to draft.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: approval for Aurora offer structure (discount vs pass-through)

Approve with modification — we can present Offer A to Aurora but with a tighter cap and a contractual contingency:
- Approve Offer A with 20% discount, 12-month term, index-linked pass-through with 3-month lookback.
- Change: pass-through threshold = 10% above baseline (not 12%) and cap = +15% over baseline (not 20%).
- Add automatic quarterly review clause and right to switch to Offer B if index volatility exceeds 18% for two consecutive quarters.

Naomi — please update the term sheet and produce a clean "offer term sheet" PDF. Vivek — you can share the modified Offer A term sheet with Aurora and label it as "subject to final contract review". Keep procurement looped.

Marissa Cole
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
